sources.entry: RktMachine - Menu bar macOS app for running rkt in a macOS hypervisor CoreOS VM.

summary.one_liner: RktMachine is a macOS menu bar app that runs a CoreOS virtual machine via HyperKit and the macOS Hypervisor for developing and running software with the rkt container system.
summary.what_it_does: The app runs a CoreOS VM on macOS using HyperKit and the macOS Hypervisor framework, and manages it from a dog-silhouette menu bar icon. On start, it boots an existing CoreOS VM or creates and boots a new one. It can open SSH sessions to the VM from the menu. The current user's home directory is mounted from the host into the VM at the same path. The README describes it as a combination of coreos-osx and corectl.app, integrated into one app with fewer configuration options. It is intended to provide a container environment with the dependencies a project needs, using rkt.
use_cases: run rkt containers on a Mac
provide a CoreOS VM for development dependencies
try out new tools and services quickly in a container VM
build and run software inside a container environment on macOS
manage a local CoreOS VM from the menu bar
how_to_run: Download the dmg from the releases page
Open the dmg and copy RktMachine.app to /Applications
Launch RktMachine; enter your user password when prompted to start the corectl service as root
Use the menu bar dog icon to manage the VM and SSH into it
To develop: open the RktMachine Xcode project and use Product -> Run
notable: Menu bar app that boots and manages a CoreOS VM on macOS
Mounts the host user home directory into the VM at the same path
Combines coreos-osx and corectl.app into one app
caveats: Configurability is reduced by design compared with the upstream coreos-osx and corectl.app tools
Requires the user password to start the corectl service as root
Built with Xcode, so development builds need Xcode
